messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: near positive definite function
parts:
On Tuesday, December 3, 2013 9:10:42 PM UTC-5, KK Sasa wrote:
Will Stan offer a  function like 'nearPD' function in R?
Can it  run efficiently if I code it in Stan by myself?

I don't think it is a good idea to have such a function. If the covariance matrix is fixed, then you can do some sort of a transformation of the small eigenvalues before passing it to Stan (or you can do it in transformed data if you want). If the covariance matrix is a parameter, then declaring it to be a cov_matrix or a corr_matrix or using an appropriate construction algorithm will guarantee that it is positive definite. We do have a problem in Stan where the tolerance for rejecting a matrix that is barely positive definite is too strict, but that will just result in some proposals being rejected, which is generally not a big deal.

Mike is doing something similar with a softabs transformation of the eigenvalues of the Hessian in the RMHMC branch, but that is a bit of a different animal (because the Hessian is actually indefinite at some points in the posterior distribution) and I doubt any of that would get exposed into the modeling language.

Ben
